classification.difficultyReason: Connect quartiles dividing observations into equal proportions with unequal numerical spreads to explain why the median can lie off-centre.

content.prompt: In a boxplot, why is the median not always in the centre of the box?

answer.short: The values between the lower quartile and median may have a different spread from those between the median and upper quartile.
answer.worked: The box extends from the lower quartile to the upper quartile. Each side of the median represents about 25% of the data, but these values need not have the same spread. Therefore, the distances from the median to the two quartiles need not be equal.
